title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1986 notes on 'ateliers' (workshops) and 'magasins' (stores). These are a combinatorial, point-free axiomatization of tame or stratified geometry, in the line of the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme. An atelier A carries a set Σ = Σ_A of 'supports' (closed or locally closed pieces). Inside it sits the subcategory Σ_cons of constructible supports, together with figures and their subdivisions. On the previous page Grothendieck distrusts arguments that rely on supports. He asks whether one can 'expliciter une construction indépendante de la notion préalable de Σ, le mal-aimé' ('give an explicit construction independent of the prior notion of Σ, the unloved one').

This page makes the question concrete. Take a 'relative' magasin-atelier F with its order or refinement relation ≪. Can the constructible sets be recovered from (F, ≪) alone? Can the 'ensemble adonné' (an ordered or lattice-like structure attached to Σ) be obtained by 'inverting' the subdivision arrows ↞, that is, by forming a category of fractions?

Modern reading: localize the category of figures/subdivisions at the class of subdivision maps. The hope is that this localization, or a filtered colimit over refinements of the face-posets or subcomplex-lattices, recovers the lattice or Boolean algebra of constructible supports. This is analogous to recovering the Boolean algebra of semialgebraic or o-minimal definable sets as a colimit over triangulations, or PL spaces as simplicial complexes with subdivisions inverted.

He admits two gaps. He has not checked that the category of fractions is an 'ensemble adonné', i.e. essentially a poset of the right type. Still less has he checked that it embeds as a sub-ensemble-adonné of Σ. He adds that this would not necessarily be bad if Σ were to be 'written off as a loss' ('largué aux profits et pertes').

He then reassures himself. When Σ is Boolean, nothing is wrong with Σ: this covers pre-Boolean ateliers, perhaps the same as the 'faithful' ateliers, or at least the magasins. He notes that this already covers all cases that interest him. The page then flows into p.122: his 'orders', pseudo-simplicial and topological structures where 'lieux' (places) replace points. He wants a direct description of Σ in the spirit of a 'géométrie des formes' (geometry of shapes), and lists next tasks: sub-ateliers and morphisms, moderate ateliers, saturation axioms.
errors: No mathematical error; the page is openly conjectural. The two key claims are explicitly flagged as unchecked: that the category of fractions is an ordered set ('adonné'), and that it embeds in Σ.
A category of fractions obtained by inverting subdivisions need not be a poset (it can carry non-trivial automorphisms or parallel arrows). The worry is legitimate and the claim is unproven.

ideas.what: Recover the lattice of constructible supports intrinsically by inverting subdivision maps (category of fractions) on figures of a magasin-atelier, avoiding a prior notion of support Σ
ideas.modern_name: Localization at subdivisions / colimit over triangulations; point-free reconstruction of the Boolean algebra of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (subdivision-invariance: Whitehead, Zeeman); o-minimal triangulation (van den Dries); localization of simplicial complexes at subdivisions in various forms
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for a tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); ateliers are unpublished

ideas.what: When Σ is Boolean (pre-Boolean ateliers, conjecturally = faithful ateliers, or at least magasins), Σ is unproblematic
Conjectural equivalence: pre-Boolean ateliers = faithful ateliers

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes defining the poset or Boolean algebra of constructible pieces of a tame 'space' purely combinatorially, as the category of fractions of figures with subdivisions inverted. He leaves open whether the result is a poset and whether it embeds in Σ.
missed.quote: l'ensemble adonné déduit de (F, ≪) en "inversant" les "flèches" ↞ (sur les subdivisions)? Je ne me suis pas assuré que la cat. des fractions obtenue soit bien un ens. adonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to point-free or combinatorial foundations of tame topology: o-minimal spectra, and recovering definable-set algebras from triangulation data. The idea is natural, but the specific atelier formalism is undeveloped in the literature.

missed.claim: Conjecture that 'pre-Boolean' ateliers coincide with 'faithful' ateliers.
missed.quote: ateliers pré-booléens, et peut-être = les ateliers fidèles?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This only matters within the unpublished atelier theory, so its impact is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a methodological musing inside the unpublished atelier/tame-topology project. The idea of inverting subdivisions to get intrinsic constructible structure is natural and has classical analogues. It is interesting only as documentation of the project, not as a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'notion préalable de Σ, le mal-aimé ?' (not 'préadditive'); it continues 'une construction indépendante de la' from the previous page.
'les ensembles constr. (relatif : un magasin-atelier F)': the struck word above 'relatif' appears to be 'exhaustif' or similar.
'pourront-ils s'obtenir, ou pourrait-on obtenir l'ensemble adonné déduit de (F, ≪) en "inversant" les "flèches" ↞ (sur les ou "subdivisions")?'
'(Ce ne serait pas là nécessairement un mal, si Σ devait être largué aux profits et pertes...)'.
'Je dirais quand-même, pour me rassurer, que dans les cas où Σ est booléen' (the duplicated 'univers' line is spurious).
'ou tout au moins les magasins), il n'y a rien à lui reprocher. Ça inclut quand même déjà tous les cas qui me parlent.'
